title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: U is a geometrically connected hyperbolic ('anabélienne') curve over a field K of finite type over Q, with smooth compactification X = Û and cusp set I = Û \ U. Γ = Gal(K̄/K), π = π_1(U_K̄) (geometric fundamental group), and (1) is the extension 1→π→π_1(U)→Γ→1. Each cusp i has a conjugacy class of inertia subgroups L_i ≅ Ẑ(1). If i is K-rational, its decomposition group gives an extension (2) 1→L_i→D_i→Γ→1, and splittings of (2) give 'cuspidal' sections of (1).

The page opens by finishing an argument from p.54. There Grothendieck assumes the fixed-point statement (3) π^{Γ^0} = L_i for a cuspidal section. Here Γ^0 is presumably an open subgroup, or the kernel of the cyclotomic character (see errors). From (3) he deduces that the conjugacy class of a cuspidal section determines the conjugacy class of L_i, hence the cusp i. This is a workaround for the case of type (0,3), where filling two holes leaves type (0,1) and no injectivity result is available.

Conjecture A is the section conjecture for affine as well as projective hyperbolic curves, including cuspidal sections. Every section of (1) either comes from a point of U(K), or comes from a splitting of an extension (2) at a K-rational cusp i ∈ I(K̄)^Γ.

He then passes to the limit over all dense opens U of X, i.e. to the absolute Galois group E_L of the function field L. E_L → E_K is viewed as a 'groupe à lacets infini', with infinitely many conjugacy classes of loop/inertia subgroups L_i, one for each closed point. The consequence is the birational section conjecture: every splitting of E_L → E_K comes from a splitting of a decomposition-group extension of type (2) at some i ∈ X(K). Conjugacy classes of such splittings should then recover X(K), and X(K') for finite K'/K.

The margin records the expected dichotomy:
- π^{Γ_0} = (1) for sections coming from rational points (first case);
- π^{Γ_0} = L_i for cuspidal sections (second case).

This gives an intrinsic group-theoretic test separating the two kinds of section, via the centralizer of the image of Γ^0. The next page develops this test and declares the birational structure E_L → E_K 'the richest a priori'. It is the more convenient one in genus 0 and 1, where removing points kills the continuous automorphism group. The page serves the anabelian programme: a Galois-theoretic description of rational points, and reconstruction of curves from fundamental-group extensions.
errors: If Γ^0 meant an arbitrary open subgroup of Γ, then π^{Γ^0} = L_i would be false. Γ acts on L_i ≅ Ẑ(1) through the cyclotomic character, which has no nontrivial invariants over any open subgroup. For the margin dichotomy to be correct, Γ^0 must be the kernel of the cyclotomic character (Gal(K̄/K(μ_∞))) or similar; the page does not specify. With Γ^0 open, both cases would give (1) and the test would not distinguish them.
The type (0,3) gap (filling two holes gives type (0,1), with no injectivity) is acknowledged rather than resolved. Distinctness of cusp classes is made conditional on the unproven (3).

The passage to the limit needs a compactness argument: a coherent system of sections over all U, each of point or cusp type, must define a single point of X(K). This is tacitly assumed. In the limit every rational point is a cusp of some U, so all birational sections are 'cuspidal'; this is consistent with writing I^Γ = X̂(K).

ideas.what: Conjecture A: section conjecture for affine hyperbolic curves over fields finitely generated over Q, with cuspidal sections included
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings 27.6.1983; alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Passage to the limit over dense opens: splittings of E_L→E_K come from decomposition groups of K-rational points of X
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings); later studied by Koenigsmann, Pop, Esnault–Wittenberg, Stix

ideas.what: Distinguishing point sections from cuspidal sections by fixed points/centralizers of the image of Γ^0: trivial versus the inertia L_i
ideas.modern_name: Centralizers of sections / cuspidal versus non-cuspidal criterion (cf. Nakamura, Mochizuki, Stix on centralizers of decomposition groups)

ideas.what: Viewing E_L as a 'loop group' with infinitely many classes of loop subgroups; birational structure as the richest object, useful in genus 0 and 1
ideas.modern_name: Birational anabelian geometry / profinite groups with inertia structure

missed.claim: The page is an early (Longue Marche, c.1981) handwritten formulation of the section conjecture, including the cuspidal case and its birational form. It predates the 1983 Faltings letter usually cited as the origin.
missed.quote: Conjecture A Soit U courbe alg. anabélienne géom. connexe sur un corps K de type fini sur Q. Alors toute section de (1) est d'un des deux types précédents
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical dating: it shows the conjecture, including cuspidal sections and the birational version, already explicit in the Longue Marche notes.

missed.claim: The expected dichotomy π^{Γ^0} = (1) for point sections versus π^{Γ^0} = L_i for cuspidal sections is proposed as a key question ('questions-clefs'). It would give an intrinsic criterion for the type of a section, and is used to separate cusp classes in the problematic type (0,3) case.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Centralizer and fixed-point properties of sections over the cyclotomic tower are close to later work (Nakamura, Mochizuki's cuspidalization, Stix). Grothendieck's explicit formulation as a section-type criterion is a minor but specific unpublished detail.

deep.surprise_reason: The section conjecture and its birational variant are well known and credited to Grothendieck. The new elements are early dating and the explicit fixed-point dichotomy (trivial versus inertia) as a criterion for section type, a modest unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: 'i ∈ I_x(K̄)^Γ' is probably 'i ∈ I(K̄)^Γ' (the set of K-rational cusps).
'(E_L pro-cha[?]' likely reads '(E_L pouvant être' or similar: 'E_L ... considéré comme un groupe à lacets "infini"'.
Margin likely reads 'Il y a plus d'espoir [pour] les précisions π^{Γ^0} = (1) (premier cas), π^{Γ^0} = L_i (deux. cas)'.
'i ∈ I^Γ = X̂(K)' — the hat may be a correction over X; the meaning is X(K), with X = Û.
